中文書名 / Chinese Title: 城市能源自主性與極端環境韌性極限 65/90 | PART III | Research Working Edition v1.0 English Title: Urban Energy Autonomy and Extreme-Environment Resilience at the Limit This prospective STARLI research monograph asks whether a scaled district energy system can preserve minimum critical services during prolonged low sunlight, coupled storms, component outages and disconnection from external supply. Its research core couples energy autonomy, extreme-climate stress and resilience engineering. The permitted study systems are unoccupied microgrid hardware-in-the-loop benches, scaled resource components, independently metered control channels and auditable digital twins. It does not claim operational autonomy for a city or safety certification for inhabited infrastructure. The primary falsifiable claim is that a preregistered multi-source energy and priority-load coordination policy can improve net lifecycle energy yield without worsening actual critical-load loss-of-service time relative to competent fixed-rule microgrid dispatch under identical generation, storage, weather, sensor, computation, maintenance, personnel and energy budgets. Hidden imports, curtailed essential demand, oversized storage, unmetered cooling and selective failure exclusion are explicit rival accounts. Blind test assignments include forecast shifts, islanding events, battery thermal drift and correlated low-renewable conditions; physical frequency, thermal and essential-load stops override all average performance gains. The volume follows an exact 777-page working architecture: one cover, 14 research-foundation pages, 30 distinct candidate equation plates, 82 chapter introductions with 410 independent one-page investigations, 200 individual Research Gates, 33 conceptually different Phoenix Answer Embryos and seven research-closure pages. The research program includes port-level energy conservation, usable reserve after aging, Markov transition qualification, islanding survivability, weather dependence, tail-risk metrics, protection interlocks, second-team failure reconstruction and intergenerational maintenance. These are proposed test designs and existing mathematical methods deployed in a new research context, not newly discovered natural laws. Relevant external evidence includes published microgrid-controller hardware-in-the-loop research (DOI 10.1109/TCST.2024.3378989), resilience-oriented scheduling with a probability of successful islanding (10.1049/esi2.70034), ice-storm microgrid formation (10.1109/TSG.2025.3611876), microgrid design with climate-informed multiyear uncertainty (10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.123355) and energy-system resilience reviews (10.1016/j.rser.2021.111476). Other references and their exact metadata are recorded in the separate DOI Evidence Register. The two Flagship-13 Zenodo lineage DOIs are author-supplied and remain unverified in this edition; the cited studies do not validate the new F65 integrated design. This document is a Research Working Edition, not an empirical result report or a completed sixfold-QA-certified scientific monograph. Page count, bookmark structure and representative visual output are machine-checked. Recurrent editorial language and incomplete independent formula review remain disclosed limitations; the >100,000 substantively independent English-word scientific-content threshold has not been certified. STARLI / Research Institute XXXVI / 33 / 2026-11-01. Cross-flagship research interfaces: F64, F66 and F05.
